$comment: Explanation devices: which runtime device to use for which narrator job. Read by `studio.py validate` (storyboard scene `device`), docs/explanation-devices.md (the handbook) and the story-writer, motion-graphics-designer and visual-director skills. Chosen by the 2026-11-28 technique-scope council from the 96 reference technique records: about 13 devices picked by narration job, the rest kept as rules or recipes. Edit here, then run `python tests/test-studio.py` and `python scripts/studio.py validate <slug>`.

jobs.hook-headline: Open a film or section with the claim in two short lines or a word build.
jobs.introduce-term: Name a new term or object and show what it refers to.
jobs.build-up: Assemble a whole (a formula, a definition, a system) part by part as the narrator names each part.
jobs.compare: Set two things side by side and show the difference that matters.
jobs.trace-cause: Show that changing one thing changes another (an input drives an output, one view drives another).
jobs.process-step: Walk through the steps of a process or the parts of a system, one at a time.
jobs.change-over-time: Show a value or a shape changing as time passes.
jobs.rank-over-time: Show who leads and how the order changes over time.
jobs.system-running: Let a system run so the viewer watches its behaviour emerge (bursts, queues, limits, recovery).
jobs.demo-interaction: Show how someone uses an interface: type, press, toggle, get feedback.
jobs.correct-myth: State a common belief, strike it, and replace it with the correct one.
jobs.change-chapter: Turn from one section to the next so the viewer feels the reset.

devices.use_when: A claim splits into a set-up and a punch line of five words or fewer each.
devices.avoid_when: Line 2 is longer than line 1, or the accent colour is already used elsewhere on screen.

devices.use_when: The narrator speaks a short phrase word by word and each word adds meaning; snap each word to its spoken time.
devices.avoid_when: The phrase has more than about seven words or wraps onto two lines.

devices.use_when: A formula is explained term by term while a figure shows each part; ring the final term when the result lands.
devices.avoid_when: No figure shows the terms (the equation then reads as a caption), or the formula has more than about six terms.

devices.use_when: One quantity seen two ways at once: a rotation and its height, a cause and its graph over time.
devices.avoid_when: The two views are not driven by the same variable.

devices.call: Studio.comp.slider(parent, {min, max, value, step, scale|map, input, output, caveat})
devices.use_when: "If you change X, Y changes by this much": one input, one output, a clear end value held at least 1 s.
devices.avoid_when: The relationship has more than one input, or the end value is not the point.

devices.call: Studio.comp.simulation(parent, {capacity, events: Studio.comp.simulationScript(seed, phases), regimes, duration})
devices.use_when: A system's behaviour only makes sense when watched running (rate limiters, queues, caches, buffers); name each regime in the caption.
devices.avoid_when: More than about 10 events a second, or no regime captions.

devices.use_when: The story is who overtakes whom over time; at most about 8 bars.
devices.avoid_when: Only the end ranking matters (use a sorted bar chart), or steps are faster than about 0.25 s.

devices.use_when: Several parts stay on one stage and the narrator walks through them; one focus change per step, named in the caption.
devices.avoid_when: More than about 7 items, or each step needs a different picture (use scenes).

devices.use_when: A system laid out as a map larger than the frame; the camera visits each part and pulls back to the whole at the end.
devices.avoid_when: Fewer than three stops, or text that needs reading while the camera moves.

devices.use_when: A line of copy beside a demo changes as the narration moves on; pass the measured words so each swap lands in a pause.
devices.avoid_when: No measured words yet (time it after build-audio and captions --timing words).

devices.use_when: Showing how a generic interface is used: a field types, a cursor moves and clicks, a toggle flips, a notice arrives.
devices.avoid_when: Recreating a real product's interface or brand.

devices.use_when: A small tile opens into the detail it stands for (a card into its contents, an icon into its system).
devices.avoid_when: The tile and the card are not the same object.

devices.use_when: The narrator states a belief and then corrects it; the struck claim stays readable while the correction types in.
devices.avoid_when: The claim is not actually wrong (use compare).

devices.use_when: A section turn; put the title start on the first word of the next phrase so the dip sits in the narration pause.
devices.avoid_when: Every scene change (it slows the film), or a hold over 0.5 s.

existing.$comment: Runtime pieces that already serve a job; a scene may name one of these ids as its device too.

not_under_narration.$comment: Devices that must sit in a narration pause or over music only. validate warns when a scene with narration lists one in capabilities or transition_out.capability (catalogue ids) or names the technique.

film_rules.$comment: A film reads as designed when a few devices recur with meaning, not when every scene shows a new trick.
